Elaine (PM): Quick sync — handing off the design partner recruitment ops to ProdOps. Need a short checklist and SLA for responses so Sales can stop pinging me every morning.
Sophia (ProdOps): Got it. Can you list the must-haves we need in the invite before I spin up the channel?
Elaine (PM): 1) short pitch + expected time commitment, 2) screener link, 3) NDA mention, 4) kickoff window options, 5) success metrics we’ll track.
Matt (Eng): Also add "expected infra access" and privacy tier (hosted vs dedicated/private) — some partners will need explicit network details.
Samir (Design): For pitch please include one screenshot of the UI and a 30s use-case. Keeps drop-off low.
Jordan (Research): We should attach the eval prompt set example and the baseline metrics so partners know what we’re measuring.
Elaine (PM): Agreed. Sophia — can you draft the invite template? Keep it <= 4 short bullets.
Sophia (ProdOps): Drafted, posting snippet below — can you thumbs up or edit quickly?
Sophia (ProdOps): ```Hi {name}, we’re running a short private beta of Redwood Inference to test latency/cost tradeoffs for your use case. Time: ~3 sessions (30–45m) over 6 weeks. We’ll share early rollouts and prioritized fixes. Reply to accept or ask Qs. Screener: https://go.redwood/screener NDA: standard link.```
Matt (Eng): Suggest adding "data handling: no customer data retained" line to the template, some legal asks will filter out otherwise.
Samir (Design): And add a small note: "you’ll get a token stipend + priority support" — clear incentive.
Elaine (PM): Good. Now SLA: ProdOps handles first reply within 24h, engineering triage within 48h for technical blockers, and product to decide go/no-go on any scope asks within 72h. OK?
Matt (Eng): 48h triage is doable for obvious blockers. For infra-heavy asks we might need the Dedicated team; call them out in the triage doc.
Sophia (ProdOps): I'll create a short triage matrix. Where should we store it?
Elaine (PM): Put it in Confluence under "DP-onboarding/ops" and add a short README in the channel. Use the tag dp-onboard in the channel name.
devops-bot: Channel created: #dp-onboard-2024 — posting link to Confluence template.
Sophia (ProdOps): Done — Confluence link: https://go.redwood/confluence/dp-onboarding. I added checklist, triage matrix, invite template, and a sample screener.
Jordan (Research): Quick note on success metrics: please capture baseline latency p50/p95, tokens per request, fail rate, and subjective quality delta for the eval prompts.
Elaine (PM): I’ll add launch criteria: 5 engaged partners, <200ms p50 on hosted test, no P0 regressions after two weeks, and documented follow-up plan.
Matt (Eng): Can we add a fallback plan: if latency > target we automatically roll partners to a compatible smaller model variant? We should document that in the runbook.
Samir (Design): Also capture partner feedback cadence: weekly short pulse + end-of-cohort interview. I can draft the pulse form.
Sophia (ProdOps): I’ll tag all tasks in the channel and create assignees. Primary steward: @Sophia, backup: @Matt.
Elaine (PM): Thanks — I’ll ping Sales and Solutions with the new invite copy and ask them to route suitable partners here.
Matt (Eng): One more: include a quick command snippet to repro locally for partners who want to test.
Matt (Eng): ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"prompt":"<test>"}'```
Sophia (ProdOps): That’s in the Confluence doc too. Closing the loop: I’ll post a final checklist in 1h and mark the channel ready. :white_check_mark:
Elaine (PM): Perfect — thanks everyone. I’ll monitor first responses this week and escalate if anything blocks the SLA.
